gen-gf-oxanium-gf-cal-sans: Big lowercase, sharp daylight in every curve. Cal Sans follows with one stroke width and short ascenders, so a long page of sans-serif text feels friendly and easy to move through.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-carlito: Oxanium's display strokes run from stem to terminal without any swell, while Carlito brings rounder, tighter sans letters beneath. Text stays clear and compact.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-changa: Tall lowercase gives Oxanium a bold, machined stance, like neon tubing bent into letters. And Changa matches that stature, its plain sans lowercase standing firm under the heading.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-courier-prime: Uninterrupted monoline strokes and curves that end in open daylight give Oxanium its engineered, slightly futuristic look. Courier Prime's drafting-pen line answers underneath.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-days-one: Days One fills the line with its tall x-height and rope-ladder spacing, a sturdy sans-serif partner for Oxanium's stencil-cut constancy. Bigger sizes probably suit it best.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-epunda-sans: Oxanium draws every stem, bowl and tail like rope. Epunda Sans reads smoothly beneath it, a plain sans with oversized, daylight-filled counters that keep paragraphs open and easy going.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-farro: Approachable, with a spine of steel. Oxanium's tall lowercase leads, and Farro's compressed ascenders and contrast-free sans strokes keep the text beneath it quietly in step.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lays its letters out like nails on a ruler, with no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye under Oxanium's heading. Fragment Mono keeps paragraphs ticking along in an orderly, steady rhythm.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-geist-mono: Structured and precise, Oxanium makes big, short headings feel engineered, its monoline curves open to the light. But Geist Mono's code-style letters, with their generous side gaps, handle everything after.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-genos: Genos reads tight and fluent, its high midline and closely pressed sans glyphs never snagging on a closed bowl. And Oxanium's fixed-pressure strokes above it keep a long page moving without friction.
